summary_paragraph: A male patient, status post liver transplant with a history of biliary stricture treated with stent placement, was readmitted 10 days after discharge for failure to thrive and postprandial abdominal pain. He reported decreased oral intake, early satiety, and intermittent supraumbilical discomfort. Imaging confirmed stable biliary stents and no acute abdominal process, though a small fluid area near the duodenum was noted. A post-pyloric Dobhoff tube was placed under fluoroscopic guidance, and enteral feeding was initiated successfully. Chronic right-sided pain, possibly neuropathic, improved with nortriptyline and a Lidoderm patch, while gabapentin was discontinued to reduce polypharmacy. Depression and insomnia were addressed with an increased dose of mirtazapine. Myfortic replaced mycophenolate mofetil due to gastrointestinal side effects. The patient stabilized, tolerated tube feeds, and was discharged home with instructions for ongoing nutrition, medication management, and follow-up.
